purpose: A practical ranked shortlist of simulation engines for cross-scale organism design, with the status of each ON THIS PROJECT. Not a literature survey. Twelve entries, chosen to cover soft voxel mechanics, cells and morphogenesis, bioelectric, continuum/mechano/fluid, molecular, and differentiation/controller search without duplicating an engine that already works here.

ranking_for_this_project.why: already building and running here on CPU in seconds, with analytic controls that pass at ratio 1.0000 and mutants that fail. It is the only soft-body engine in this list with a receipt.

BSD-3, actively maintained (release 1.14.2), off-lattice cells plus a diffusive transport solver, and it covers the cell-mechanics-plus-substrate coupling that Morpheus's lattice formulation does not. Highest-value NEW install.
LGPL-3.0 forward soft-robot FEM on an LGPL-2.1 core, and the only route in this list from a continuum constitutive law to actuator control. Large build.
the engine the computationally designed organism results actually used, and the only GPU path for the voxel line. Blocked here, probe specified.
MIT, release 4.10.0, Potts plus SBML plus PDE. Overlaps Morpheus substantially, so it earns a slot only if a Morpheus limitation is named first.
the inverse control capability is real and directly relevant, but it is AGPL-3.0 carrying an Inria patent grant scoped to this software. Licence review precedes any use.
reads voxcraft .history files; the cheap way to animate voxel results if we adopt that format.
the original design pipeline, and the clearest statement of the evolutionary search loop. Python 2.7 plus Qt4 makes it a porting project, not a step.

engines.name: Voxelyze

license_evidence.detail: declared verbatim in every src/*.cpp and include/*.h header: 'Voxelyze is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public License ... either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.'
license_evidence.trap: there is NO LICENSE file at this commit, so the GitHub API reports license: null. That means 'no detectable LICENSE file', not 'unlicensed'. The per-file headers are the licence of record.
license_evidence.our_distribution: we commit driver source and a build recipe; no linked binary is redistributed

engines.scale: mesoscale soft body, 1e-3 to 1e-1 m, lattice of cubic voxels

governing_equations.consequence: each link is an Euler-Bernoulli beam element of length L=s with I = s^4/12, which is why a chain of them reproduces F L^3/(3EI) exactly rather than approximately. Verified here at ratio 1.0000.
governing_equations.damping: global damping C = zeta*2*sqrt(m*k), k = E*nomSize   [include/VX_Material.h:94]
governing_equations.integration: explicit Euler; doTimeStep returns false when any link axialStrain exceeds 100   [src/Voxelyze.cpp:251-269]
governing_equations.contact: rigid floor at z=0 plus optional voxel-voxel collision; Coulomb static/kinetic friction coefficients per material

supported_couplings: relative temperature -> zero-stress volumetric strain -> shape, force and motion
friction and floor contact -> ground reaction

compute.cpu: yes, single-threaded by default; USE_OMP enables OpenMP
compute.deps: g++ only; no boost, no cmake, no CUDA
compute.measured_runtime: 0.44-8.6 s per run of this project's bodies (36-360 voxels, 1.5 s simulated)

engines.build_gotcha: the upstream makefile's default FLAGS contain -DPARDISO_5=1, which leaves undefined references to pardisoinit/pardiso in the archive; any program linking it fails without a commercial Pardiso 5 library. Override FLAGS to drop the define.
applicability_limits: linear-elastic lattice with a fixed cubic topology; no remeshing, no growth, no cell division
global damping is damping to a stationary ABSOLUTE frame, not a fluid model; no swimming interpretation is available
no fluid, no diffusion, no chemistry, no electrophysiology
explicit Euler requires dt below recommendedTimeStep and diverges loudly rather than silently
no RNG anywhere, so there are no stochastic replicates and no seed spread may be reported as uncertainty
parameter_gaps: no measured biological value for coefficient of thermal expansion as an actuation proxy
no measured contractile strain amplitude or frequency for any cell type
friction against a real substrate is unmeasured; mu_s=1.0 and mu_k=0.8 are inherited from a voxcraft demo file, not from an experiment
internal, global and collision damping ratios are engineering choices
public_examples: the three-voxel cantilever in the upstream README
our six-pattern comparison and analytic controls in artifacts/voxel-actuation/
controls_available: free thermal expansion against the zero-stress law (exact)
end-loaded cantilever against F L^3/(3EI) (exact at n<=4 with a settling bound)
frictionless arm: horizontal centre-of-mass motion must be zero by conservation

engines.name: voxcraft-sim (Voxelyze 3.0)
engines.version: CMake library target is named voxelyze.3.0

license_evidence.detail: LICENSE at the pin is the Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal text; GitHub API agrees
license_evidence.CONFLICT: the project website https://cdorgs.github.io/code states verbatim 'The source code and build instructions are distributed under an Attribution-NonCommercial Creative Commons license' and links CC BY-NC 4.0. The website and the repository LICENSE file disagree. Rely on the LICENSE file in the repository you clone and record that the website says otherwise. Do not quote only the convenient one.

engines.scale: same as Voxelyze; designed for population-scale parallel evaluation

state_variables.note: expected to mirror Voxelyze's voxel state; the CUDA sources under src/VX3 were NOT read

governing_equations.named_by_build: the CMake library target is voxelyze.3.0 and src/old/ is present, so this is a CUDA re-implementation of the Voxelyze model rather than a different physics. That is an inference from the build file, not a reading of the kernels.

supported_couplings: per-material temperature phase offset (MaterialTempPhase in the VXA format), which is the per-voxel actuation phase that Voxelyze 0.9 lacks

compute.cpu: no, CUDA is a required project language
compute.gpu: required at BUILD time as well as run time: CMakeLists.txt autodetects the architecture by probing a GPU and takes the newest found
compute.deps: CUDA toolkit with nvcc hardcoded at /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc, Boost (filesystem thread chrono program_options, static), CMake >= 3.12, C++17
compute.declared_cuda: README says CUDA 10.1; Dockerfile pins nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:10.2-devel-ubuntu18.04. These disagree.
compute.measured_on_a_modern_toolkit: does not compile under CUDA 13.1 for sm_90 at this pin

engines.blocker: MEASURED, not inferred: job aijob-e00wfnzb38fccw6k57 on an H100 returned COMPILE_FAIL in 39.0 s under CUDA 13.1 / CMake 3.31.6 / g++ 13.3.0 targeting sm_90. src/VX3/VX3_VoxelyzeKernel.cu produces 16 errors at 8 sites, all of the form 'calling a __host__ function("cudaDeviceSynchronize") from a __device__ function ... is not allowed'. That is legacy CUDA dynamic parallelism, removed in CUDA 12.0. It is in upstream's source and no image change fixes it. A separate and EARLIER failure in the same build, on Boost.Asio in VX3_SimulationManager.cu, was caused by OUR adapter installing Boost 1.83 against an upstream README that names 1.65.1 and 1.67.0; the two failures are in different translation units and neither caused the other. No simulation ran, so nothing is established about the engine's physics. See artifacts/voxcraft-gpu-probe/result.json.
applicability_limits: last pushed 2022-08-09; the CUDA-10-era device code against a current toolchain is an open question, not a known failure
arch autodetection emits SASS only, so running a 10.2-built binary on a newer GPU needs an explicit PTX gencode for forward JIT
public_examples: demos/basic/base.vxa and robot.vxd at the pin; base.vxa supplies Lattice_Dim 0.01 m, Elastic_Mod 1e5 Pa, Density 1e3 kg/m3, Poissons_Ratio 0.35, CTE 0, uStatic 1, uDynamic 0.8, which this project adopted as sourced baseline parameters
a read-only Google Colab notebook linked from the README

controls_available.note: src/Executables/vx3_test.cu exists; its contents were not read

engines.name: PhysiCell (with BioFVM)
engines.category: cells and morphogenesis; off-lattice agents plus diffusive transport

version_evidence.detail: VERSION.txt reads 1.14.2; the latest GitHub release is tagged 1.14.2, published 2025-01-20

license_evidence.detail: licenses/PhysiCell.txt is the BSD 3-Clause text, 'Copyright (c) 2016-2021, Paul Macklin and the PhysiCell Project'. The GitHub API reports license: null because there is no LICENSE file at the repository ROOT - the same trap as Voxelyze, with the opposite conclusion about permissiveness. Separate licence files exist for BioFVM, MaBoSS and pugixml, so a reuser must check all four.

engines.scale: 10^-5 to 10^-3 m; 10^5-10^6 cells with a coupled substrate field

state_variables.named_by_verified_title: the venue title is 'an open source physics-based cell simulator for 3-D multicellular systems', and BioFVM's is 'an efficient, parallelized diffusive transport solver for 3-D biological simulations'. Cell positions, volumes, phenotype state and substrate concentration fields follow from those titles; the EQUATIONS were not read here.
state_variables.next_to_open: the PhysiCell paper 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005991 and the BioFVM paper 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv730

supported_couplings: cell mechanics (off-lattice, so shape is not constrained to a lattice, unlike Morpheus's CPM)
intracellular models via MaBoSS and SBML addons (addons/ directory is present at HEAD)
engines.why_it_earns_a_slot_despite_morpheus: Morpheus is a cellular Potts lattice formulation. PhysiCell is off-lattice with a separate transport solver, so it covers the cell-mechanics-plus-substrate coupling that a CPM represents only indirectly. That is a different capability, not a duplicate install.
applicability_limits: cell-type-specific rules and units must be fitted; nothing transfers from a cancer parameterisation to a fish or an amphibian construct by matching variable names
parameter_gaps: every rate, adhesion and motility parameter needs a context-matched source for any organism we care about

controls_available.note: unit_tests/ and tests/ are present; contents not read

engines.name: SOFA SoftRobots.Inverse plugin
engines.license: AGPL-3.0, with an explicit patent note

license_evidence.api_note: the GitHub API reports NOASSERTION / 'Other' because of the added clause file
license_evidence.patent_scoping_VERBATIM: The open source software "SoftRobots.Inverse" implements the patented Inria method for performing the inverse in real time in order to control the robot: Inria patent entitled "Method for controlling of a deformable robot, associated module and computer program", filed in France on 8 February 2013 (priority date) publication number: FR3002047 - 2014-08-15 - WO2014122134A1; US2015360367A1; EP2954429A1; JP2016513021A.
license_evidence.grant_scope_VERBATIM: Clause 11 of its open source license "AGPLv3" grants you a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use and exploit this patent when you use "SoftRobots.Inverse" software or any derivative software work (i.e., developed from the source of that software) to implement this patented method.
license_evidence.exclusion_VERBATIM: Any other exploitation of the patent, in particular by using a software solution to implement the method other than "SoftRobots.Inverse", not using the source code of "SoftRobots.Inverse", developed by you and/or by a third party is not covered by this license.
license_evidence.what_this_means_for_us: two separate constraints, both narrow and specific. (1) AGPL-3.0: network use triggers the source-provision obligation, which matters for a hosted service. (2) The patent grant is scoped to THIS software and its derivatives. Writing our own inverse soft-robot controller implementing the same method is explicitly NOT covered. Inria names stip-lille@inria.fr for a separate paid licence. This is a statement of what the licence files say, not legal advice, and it is not a claim about any commercial position.
license_evidence.do_not_generalise: none of this applies to the SOFA core (LGPL-2.1) or the forward SoftRobots plugin (LGPL-3.0).

supported_couplings: desired end-effector motion -> required actuator inputs, solved in real time

compute.deps: a strong dependence on the SoftRobots plugin, stated in its README

applicability_limits: inverse control of a deformable mechanism is not inverse DESIGN of an organism; it solves for actuator inputs given a model, not for a body given a goal
parameter_gaps: requires a validated forward model first
public_examples: distributed in SOFA stable binaries per its README
